content.overview: Section 20 permits parties to agree on the place of arbitration; failing agreement, the tribunal determines the place having regard to the circumstances and convenience of the parties.
content.glance: Section 20 permits parties to agree on the place of arbitration; failing agreement, the tribunal determines the place having regard to the circumstances and convenience of the parties.
content.study:
Module 1: Party choice
The parties may agree on the place of arbitration.

Module 2: Tribunal determination
If parties do not agree, the tribunal determines the place after considering the circumstances, including convenience.

Module 3: Legal significance
The place chosen under section 20 must be distinguished from the physical venue where hearings occur; the statutory and jurisprudential consequences of seat/place require careful analysis.

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: The parties agree Mumbai as the place; the tribunal ordinarily gives effect to that agreement within the Act.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: A party assumes that every hearing venue automatically changes the juridical place of arbitration.

hypotheticals.question: Why distinguish place from hearing venue?
hypotheticals.analysis: Because the juridical consequences of the chosen place are not necessarily identical to the physical venue of a particular hearing.

rows.left: The chosen place can carry juridical significance.
rows.right: A hearing may occur elsewhere for convenience.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 20 as self-contained without reading its statutory conditions.
misconceptions.correction: Apply section 20 with the Act's express conditions and connected provisions.
